arms.name: Barbell Curl
arms.regional_bias: overall biceps (fixed supinated grip; both heads loaded through big-load full ROM)

arms.name: EZ-Bar Curl
arms.regional_bias: overall biceps with slightly less supination than the straight bar (more wrist-friendly)

arms.name: Dumbbell Curl
arms.regional_bias: overall biceps; supination twist option emphasizes the supination function

arms.name: Dumbbell Twist (Supination) Curl
arms.regional_bias: biceps supination emphasis (source's named example of loading the supination function)

arms.name: Preacher Curl
arms.regional_bias: short head of biceps; heavy stretched-position loading

arms.name: Concentration Curl
arms.regional_bias: short head / peak contraction; strong supination cue

arms.name: Cable Curl
arms.regional_bias: overall biceps; constant-tension loading ideal for high-rep and drop sets

arms.name: Hammer Curl
arms.regional_bias: brachialis and brachioradialis (neutral grip removes the supination demand)

arms.name: Triceps Pushdown
arms.regional_bias: lateral and medial heads (arm at the side keeps the long head shortened)

arms.name: Rope Triceps Pushdown
arms.regional_bias: lateral and medial heads; rope spread adds end-range contraction

arms.name: Overhead Cable Rope Triceps Extension
arms.regional_bias: long head of triceps (overhead = long-head stretch bias)

arms.name: Overhead Barbell / EZ-Bar Triceps Extension
arms.regional_bias: long head of triceps (overhead stretch); heavier than the DB/cable versions

arms.name: Skullcrusher (Lying Triceps Extension)
arms.regional_bias: long and medial heads; partial long-head stretch (more if lowered behind the head)

arms.name: JM Press
arms.regional_bias: overall triceps (medial/lateral emphasis); heaviest of the triceps moves

forearms.name: Finger-Rolling Wrist Curl (Dynamic Finger Curl)
forearms.regional_bias: finger flexors (flexor digitorum) at long lengths

forearms.name: Plate Pinch Hold
forearms.regional_bias: finger flexors + thumb adductors at long lengths

glutes.name: Conventional Barbell Deadlift
glutes.regional_bias: whole posterior chain; relatively erector- and quad-dominant vs RDL/stiff-leg, with semitendinosus > biceps femoris within the hamstrings

glutes.name: Sumo Deadlift
secondary: Adductor longus and brevis (with gracilis, pectineus)
glutes.regional_bias: more quad/adductor and less lower-back demand than conventional; strong glute and adductor-magnus contribution

glutes.name: Trap-Bar (Hex-Bar) Deadlift
glutes.regional_bias: more quad-dominant and lower erector-spinae stress than straight-bar deadlift; load line through the body reduces shear

glutes.name: Deficit Deadlift
glutes.regional_bias: greater bottom-range stretch on glutes and hamstrings than floor pulls; deficit sumo is a favoured heavy compound for glute growth

glutes.name: Low-Bar Back Squat
glutes.regional_bias: more glute/hip; least rectus-femoris of the squat variants

glutes.name: Barbell Hip Thrust
glutes.regional_bias: upper gluteus maximus (highest EMG of the loaded bilateral lifts; ~82% MVIC traditional, upper GM ~87% vs lower GM ~70%)

glutes.name: American Hip Thrust
glutes.regional_bias: upper gluteus maximus (American style upper GM ~90% vs lower GM ~57% MVIC)

glutes.name: Smith Machine Hip Thrust
glutes.regional_bias: upper gluteus maximus

glutes.name: Single-Leg Hip Thrust
glutes.regional_bias: gluteus maximus + added gluteus medius (pelvic-leveling) demand

glutes.name: Barbell Glute Bridge
glutes.regional_bias: gluteus maximus (short-lever knee angle reduces hamstring share)

glutes.name: Frog Pump
glutes.regional_bias: gluteus maximus (abducted/externally-rotated setup increases GM share, reduces hamstring)

glutes.name: Cable Glute Kickback
glutes.regional_bias: gluteus maximus (lower fibers, terminal hip extension); minimal systemic/synergist fatigue so very high SFR with short rest

glutes.name: Cable Standing Hip Abduction
glutes.regional_bias: gluteus medius/minimus (frontal-plane abductors)

glutes.name: Romanian Deadlift (Glute-Biased)
glutes.regional_bias: gluteus maximus + hamstrings at long muscle length; stiff-leg/RDL hinge ~40% GMax MVIC, glute share rises with a hard lockout and posterior hip drive

glutes.name: Sumo Deficit Deadlift
glutes.regional_bias: gluteus maximus with heavy adductor magnus involvement from the wide stance; the deficit adds bottom-range stretch

glutes.name: Dumbbell Step-Up
glutes.regional_bias: gluteus maximus + gluteus medius (highest GMax EMG of any reviewed exercise; a high box biases the glute)

glutes.name: Lateral Step-Up
glutes.regional_bias: gluteus maximus with heavy gluteus medius/minimus involvement (frontal-plane stabilization)

glutes.name: Barbell Walking Lunge
glutes.regional_bias: gluteus maximus (deep lunge stretch) + gluteus medius stabilization

glutes.name: Bulgarian Split Squat (Glute-Biased)
glutes.regional_bias: gluteus maximus (lengthened position via forward lean + long stance) with gluteus medius stabilization

glutes.name: Cable Standing Hip Abduction (TFL / Minimus Bias)
glutes.regional_bias: gluteus minimus and tensor fasciae latae; raising the leg out and slightly forward (rather than out-and-back, which favors GMax/medius) emphasizes the anterior abductors. Constant cable tension through ROM.

hamstrings.name: Romanian Deadlift (RDL)
hamstrings.regional_bias: hamstring-dominant hip hinge; targets semitendinosus more than the stiff-leg deadlift does

hamstrings.name: Step (Deficit) Romanian Deadlift
hamstrings.regional_bias: highest overall posterior-chain excitation of the RDL family due to greater ROM/stretch; emphasizes semitendinosus and gluteus maximus

hamstrings.name: Stiff-Leg Deadlift (SLDL)
hamstrings.regional_bias: glute-max-biased hip hinge (more than RDL); within hamstrings, semitendinosus still > biceps femoris but less ST emphasis than RDL

hamstrings.name: Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
hamstrings.regional_bias: hamstring-dominant hip hinge; dumbbells permit a marginally larger stretch ROM than the barbell

hamstrings.name: Single-Leg Romanian Deadlift
hamstrings.regional_bias: single-leg hamstring/glute hinge with extra gluteus-medius and anti-rotation demand; strong semitendinosus emphasis

hamstrings.name: Barbell Good Morning
hamstrings.regional_bias: hamstring + spinal-erector hinge; more semitendinosus and less biceps femoris than the RDL, with heavy lower-back demand

hamstrings.name: Lying (Prone) Leg Curl
hamstrings.regional_bias: knee-flexion isolation biased toward the biceps femoris (both upper and lower portions); prone hip angle differs from seated

hamstrings.name: Seated Leg Curl
hamstrings.regional_bias: knee-flexion isolation under hip flexion (lengthened hamstring); favoured for stretch-mediated growth and high-rep work

hamstrings.name: Standing (Single-Leg) Leg Curl
hamstrings.regional_bias: unilateral knee-flexion isolation; neutral-hip position sits between the seated (flexed) and lying (extended) hamstring length profiles

chest.name: Barbell Flat Bench Press
chest.regional_bias: whole pec (balanced clavicular/sternal/costal); slight sternocostal emphasis vs incline

chest.name: Incline Barbell Bench Press
chest.regional_bias: clavicular (upper) pec; peaks ~30 deg, anterior delt takeover >45 deg

chest.name: Dumbbell Flat Bench Press
chest.regional_bias: whole pec, sternocostal emphasis; deep-stretch loaded

chest.name: Machine Chest Press
chest.regional_bias: whole pec (mid/sternal); height of handles can shift bias

chest.name: Bayesian Cable Flye
chest.regional_bias: whole pec, deep-stretch biased; matches pressing internal-rotation pattern

chest.name: Push-Up
chest.regional_bias: whole pec (lower bias); serratus-loaded via protraction

core.name: AbMat Sit-Up
core.regional_bias: whole rectus abdominis, emphasis on lengthened range

shoulders.name: Dumbbell Lateral Raise
shoulders.regional_bias: lateral (middle) deltoid; raising in the true frontal plane minimizes front-delt takeover vs scapular-plane raising

shoulders.name: Cable Lateral Raise
shoulders.regional_bias: lateral deltoid with strong loaded-stretch emphasis at the bottom

shoulders.name: Cable Cross-Body Lateral Raise
shoulders.regional_bias: lateral deltoid, loaded-stretch biased

shoulders.name: Lean-Away Dumbbell Lateral Raise
shoulders.regional_bias: lateral deltoid with bottom/stretch emphasis

shoulders.name: Cable Face Pull
shoulders.regional_bias: posterior deltoid plus external rotators (infraspinatus/teres minor) and mid-trap

shoulders.name: Bent-Over Dumbbell Rear Lateral Raise
shoulders.regional_bias: posterior deltoid

shoulders.name: Cable Cross-Body Rear Lateral Raise
shoulders.regional_bias: posterior deltoid, loaded-stretch biased

shoulders.name: Cable Cuff Lateral Raise (Grip-Bypass)
shoulders.regional_bias: lateral deltoid; grip fully bypassed

shoulders.name: Cable Cuff Rear Delt Fly (Grip-Bypass)
shoulders.regional_bias: posterior deltoid; grip fully bypassed

shoulders.name: High Row / Cable Rear-Delt Row (Elbows-Flared)
shoulders.regional_bias: rear delt, mid-traps and rhomboids — the elbows-high flared path Henselmans flags for upper-back/rear-delt bias rather than lats

shoulders.name: Cable External Rotation at 90-Degree Abduction
shoulders.regional_bias: posterior cuff (infraspinatus/teres minor) in the abducted/overhead-relevant position; complements the elbow-at-side angle for fuller cuff coverage

shoulders.name: Full-Can Raise (Supraspinatus)
shoulders.regional_bias: supraspinatus (initiates abduction in the scapular plane); the externally-rotated full-can path is the impingement-safer way to load it directly

shoulders.name: Lying Dumbbell Internal Rotation
shoulders.regional_bias: subscapularis (anterior cuff); free-weight version is light and peaks near the top of internal rotation

shoulders.name: Side-Lying Dumbbell External Rotation
shoulders.regional_bias: posterior cuff (infraspinatus/teres minor); free-weight version peaks resistance near the top of external rotation and is light by necessity

shoulders.name: Cable External Rotation (Elbow at Side)
shoulders.regional_bias: posterior rotator cuff (infraspinatus/teres minor) at the elbow-by-side angle; continuous cable tension loads the full arc better than a dumbbell

shoulders.name: Cable Internal Rotation (Elbow at Side)
shoulders.regional_bias: subscapularis (anterior cuff) at the elbow-by-side angle; internal rotators are strong, but this isolates the deep cuff component away from the lats/pecs

shoulders.name: Barbell Upright Row
shoulders.regional_bias: lateral deltoid and upper trapezius (more trap as the pull goes higher / wider abduction)

shoulders.name: Dumbbell Upright Row
shoulders.regional_bias: lateral deltoid and upper trapezius

shoulders.name: Cable Upright Row
shoulders.regional_bias: lateral deltoid and upper trapezius

shoulders.name: Standing Barbell Overhead Press
shoulders.regional_bias: anterior deltoid (also lateral deltoid when elbows flared); high systemic/core cost

shoulders.name: Seated Barbell Overhead Press
shoulders.regional_bias: anterior deltoid; lower systemic cost than standing variant

shoulders.name: Seated Dumbbell Shoulder Press
shoulders.regional_bias: anterior deltoid with deep-stretch emphasis

shoulders.name: Smith Machine Seated Shoulder Press
shoulders.regional_bias: anterior deltoid; low systemic disruption (good for higher reps)

shoulders.name: Machine Shoulder Press
shoulders.regional_bias: anterior deltoid; lowest systemic cost of the presses

shoulders.name: Dumbbell Front Raise
shoulders.regional_bias: anterior deltoid

shoulders.name: Cable Front Raise
shoulders.regional_bias: anterior deltoid, continuous-tension

back.name: Barbell Bent-Over Row (Overhand)
back.regional_bias: whole upper/mid back; overhand + flared elbows biases upper back, rhomboids, mid-traps and rear delt

back.name: Barbell Bent-Over Row (with Lifting Straps)
back.regional_bias: whole upper/mid back; grip removed as limiter so target back muscles drive failure

back.name: Pendlay Row (Dead-Stop Barbell Row)
back.regional_bias: explosive upper-back / mid-trap and rhomboid emphasis; strict torso angle limits cheating

back.name: Barbell Row (Underhand / Supinated Grip)
back.regional_bias: lower lats and teres major via the tucked, elbows-back path; greater biceps contribution

back.name: T-Bar Row (Landmine Row)
back.regional_bias: thick mid-back — rhomboids, mid-traps, teres major; neutral grip lets heavy loading with comfortable shoulder/wrist positions

back.name: Incline-Bench Chest-Supported Dumbbell Row
back.regional_bias: mid-back/lats with no lower-back demand; neutral or pronated grip selectable to shift between lat and upper-back bias

back.name: One-Arm Dumbbell Row (Bench-Supported)
back.regional_bias: lats and teres major via a long elbows-back pull; per-side loading lets you bias each lat individually

back.name: Seated Cable Row (Wide Pronated Grip)
back.regional_bias: upper back — rhomboids, mid-traps and rear delt — via the wide, elbows-flared high-row path

back.name: Seated Cable Row (Close Neutral V-Handle)
back.regional_bias: lats and teres major via the close, elbows-tucked-and-back pull

back.name: Single-Arm Seated/Half-Kneeling Cable Row
back.regional_bias: lats/teres major with extra range; allows independent per-side reach and scapular protraction at the stretch

back.name: Meadows Row (Landmine Single-Arm Row)
back.regional_bias: lats and teres major, with strong upper-back involvement; pronated grip plus the landmine arc loads the stretched position heavily

back.name: Inverted Row (Bodyweight Horizontal Row)
back.regional_bias: upper/mid back and rear delt; difficulty self-regulated by foot position, good for higher-rep upper-back work

back.name: Gorilla Row (Bent-Over Alternating Dumbbell Row)
back.regional_bias: lats and teres major with anti-rotation trunk demand; alternating single-arm loading lets each side be driven hard

back.name: Seal Row (Prone Bench Barbell/Dumbbell Row)
back.regional_bias: whole mid/upper back with zero cheat; grip strength is the main non-back limiter, which straps can remove

back.name: Smith Machine Bent-Over Row
back.regional_bias: whole mid/upper back; fixed bar path standardizes the stroke and removes stabilization, akin to the Smith prone bench pull used in strap research

back.name: Fat-Grip (Thick-Bar) Dumbbell Row
back.regional_bias: lats with added finger-flexor support-grip stimulus

back.name: Wide-Grip Lat Pulldown
back.regional_bias: upper/outer lats (wide grip emphasizes shoulder adduction; Sperandei found wide pronated grip the highest lat:biceps ratio of the pulldown variants)

back.name: Close Neutral-Grip Lat Pulldown
back.regional_bias: lower lats (close/neutral grip allows more shoulder extension, biasing lower lat fibers; neutral grip is wrist-friendly)

back.name: Reverse-Grip (Underhand) Lat Pulldown
back.regional_bias: lower lats with more biceps involvement (supination slightly raises biceps and lowers the lat:biceps ratio vs wide grip per Sperandei, but lat activation itself is statistically unchanged)

back.name: Single-Arm Cable Lat Pulldown
back.regional_bias: full lat with extended stretch range; lets each side reach an unrestricted overhead stretch and bottom contraction

back.name: Pull-Up (Pronated/Overhand)
back.regional_bias: upper/outer lats (pronated, wider hand spacing biases shoulder adduction and upper lat fibers)

back.name: Weighted Pull-Up
back.regional_bias: upper/outer lats; a primary heavy vertical-pull anchor (RP pairs weighted pull-ups with barbell rows as the heavy back staples)

back.name: Chin-Up (Supinated/Underhand)
back.regional_bias: lower lats plus heavy biceps (close supinated grip = shoulder extension; chin-ups are a notable biceps stimulus, comparable to curls)

back.name: Neutral-Grip Pull-Up
back.regional_bias: lower/mid lats with strong brachialis-brachioradialis involvement; joint-friendly intermediate between pull-up and chin-up

back.name: Straight-Arm Cable Pulldown
back.regional_bias: lats through shoulder extension with minimal arm involvement; the long head of the triceps assists as a shoulder extensor (straight-arm pulldowns can drive high long-head triceps activity)

back.name: Lat Prayer (Cable Straight-Arm Pullover with Body English)
back.regional_bias: lats through their entire length, with the greatest resistance in full contraction; matches the lat's strength curve better than rows or pulldowns and trains the long lengthened position rows omit

back.name: Dumbbell Pullover
back.regional_bias: lats and lower pec at the stretched position; trains the lengthened position rows skip but loses tension as the arms reach vertical

back.name: Behind-the-Neck Lat Pulldown
back.regional_bias: upper lats and traps; produces no more lat activation than front pulldowns while adding shoulder/neck risk, so it is a lower-priority variant

back.name: Sternum (Gironda) Chin-Up
back.regional_bias: lower lats via deep shoulder extension in the contracted position; a contraction-emphasis bodyweight vertical pull

back.name: Commando (Mixed-Grip) Pull-Up
back.regional_bias: lats with heavy oblique/core anti-rotation; the alternating-side path biases the lat on the side the head rises toward

back.name: Supine Cable Scapular Protraction (Serratus Punch)
back.regional_bias: serraty anterior (isolated open-chain protraction); pec minor assists; minimal glenohumeral motion keeps it off the delts/pec major

back.name: Serratus Punch / Scapular Push-Up (Push-Up Plus)
back.regional_bias: serratus anterior (the push-up-plus end range is its highest-activation drill); pec minor assists scapular tilt/protraction

back.name: Overhead Shrug (Scapular Upward-Rotation Shrug)
back.regional_bias: serratus anterior + upper trapezius force couple for scapular upward rotation in the overhead position; trains lockout stability for pressing

quads.name: High-Bar Back Squat
quads.regional_bias: overall quads with rectus femoris emphasis vs low-bar; deep ROM loads vastii at long length

quads.name: Front Squat
quads.regional_bias: strongest quad bias of the barbell squats; rectus femoris and vastii

quads.name: Leg Extension
quads.regional_bias: all four heads; 90-degree hip seating biases the vastii (esp. vastus lateralis) over rectus femoris

quads.name: Leg Extension (Reclined / Extended-Hip, Rectus-Femoris Bias)
quads.regional_bias: rectus femoris (especially proximal/upper) emphasis from the more extended hip

quads.name: Sissy Squat
quads.regional_bias: rectus femoris and overall quad at long muscle length; lengthened-bias exercise

quads.name: Reverse Nordic Curl
quads.regional_bias: rectus femoris at extreme length; lengthened-bias quad exercise

quads.name: Bulgarian Split Squat (Dumbbell)
quads.regional_bias: front-leg quad; upright torso = more quad, forward lean = more glute

quads.name: Bulgarian Split Squat (Barbell)
quads.regional_bias: front-leg quad with deep-ROM long-length loading

quads.name: Walking Lunge (Dumbbell)
quads.regional_bias: front-leg quad on short steps; more glute/hamstring on long steps

quads.name: Walking Lunge (Barbell)
quads.regional_bias: front-leg quad; step length shifts quad vs glute share

quads.name: Dumbbell Step-Up
quads.regional_bias: working-leg quad; higher box adds glute

quads.name: Goblet Squat
quads.regional_bias: quad-biased via upright torso and deep ROM

calves.name: Single-Leg Calf Raise (Ankle-Stabilizer Focus)
calves.regional_bias: tibialis posterior and the fibularis group as medial/lateral ankle stabilizers controlling inversion-eversion drift during a single-leg raise (gastrocnemius/soleus/plantaris drive the plantarflexion itself). Distinct from the gastroc-primary single-leg calf raise: here the goal is frontal-plane ankle control, balance, and arch/stabilizer strength.

adductors.name: Copenhagen Plank / Adduction
primary: Adductor longus and brevis (with gracilis, pectineus)
adductors.regional_bias: adductor longus/brevis and adductor magnus of the top (supporting) leg, loaded heavily in a lengthened position; doubles as anti-lateral-flexion core work. A well-supported eccentric/lengthened adductor stimulus.

adductors.name: Cable Standing Hip Adduction
primary: Adductor longus and brevis (with gracilis, pectineus)
adductors.regional_bias: adductor longus/brevis (frontal-plane adductors) with adductor magnus; single-leg loading lets the working leg start in a deep abducted stretch.
